summary:
I reviewed the proposed DFT campaign through one lens: how it links to TCAD and whether its results can be falsified. The ATLAS model's parameters and decks are read from PKG = C:\Users\moham\Downloads\IWO_Local_Codex_Handoff (1)\IWO_PHYSICS_CONSTRAINED_MODEL_V1 (config\iwo_material_model.yaml, results\runs\run_0038/0039/0040\device.in, chapters 04-13, analysis_2026-09-25). This was a read-only review; nothing was run or modified.

Bottom line: almost none of the proposed DFT-to-TCAD mappings gives an out-of-sample test against the data that exist. Only one transfer curve per thickness exists (ID-VG at Vd = 0.7 V), and on it dEc, chi, the gate work function and Qf act as one exact rigid shift (dEc(2 nm) = 0.353 eV is equivalent to 1.97e12 cm^-2). A DFT dEc(t) therefore only changes the refitted Qf. It can be inserted with zero ATLAS launches through the exact identities, and it is falsifiable only by an optical-gap or C-V measurement. SYNTHESIS.md:504 says the same.

- **m*(t) to N_C(t):** effect is second order (about 2.4 % of the threshold step).
- **Eg(t):** has no leverage, because holes are not solved.
- **V_O/W to N_D:** forbidden by the config's own provenance rule, has no effect at 2 nm (0.036 V per 1e18 cm^-3), and slab defect concentrations are far too high. One defect in the 2 nm cell is about 5e20 cm^-3 (computed). Taken literally, the W result would stop the 2 nm device from turning off.
- **Defect DOS to g_t(E) and interface dipole to Qf:** these either add fitted knobs or relabel one that is already fitted.
- **Phi_Bn to contact boundary:** the only no-knob insertion with a distinct, non-rigid signature. It needs a correction of the conduction-band minimum position (not of the gap) and a pre-registered decision window. The thermionic estimates, computed here and conditional on the model: below about 0.18 eV it cannot be told apart from Ohmic; 0.18-0.23 eV is testable only with low-Vd ID-VD data, which are not in the package; above about 0.23 eV it contradicts the existing 2 nm theta bound.
- **"Phi_Bn -> freeze -> predict I_off" and the Block 2 Pd/V_O off-floor idea:** falsified in advance.
  - No V1 run ever changed the source/drain contact potential.
  - The earlier Astra Schottky runs gave off-currents of 1e-34 to 1e-53 A/um, against measured floors of 4.6e-15 to 6.6e-12 A/um.
  - Ideal Ohmic is already the injection upper bound, and in a 20 um channel the off-current is set by the gate-controlled channel barrier, not by the contact.
  - The floors do not depend on gate voltage and scale as t^3.8.
- **6.3 and 13.2 nm crystalline slabs:** cannot address the open TCAD questions. Removing the 6.3 nm rigid offset (with Qf shared by 2 and 13.2 nm) would need about 0.36 V of realized confinement at 6.3 nm. The infinite-well upper bound there is about 0.045 eV. The m*(6.3)/m*(13.2) ratio is 1.03, against the x4.58 mobility step.
- **Most valuable DFT targets for TCAD:**
  1. dEc derived from the slab sub-band ladder (the subthreshold-equivalent shift) at 2 nm, with Nc kept at the bulk mass.
  2. The Pd barrier, but only after bulk PBE/HSE band-edge offsets relative to the average potential are computed and the unexplained vacuum-level shift of the W-doped slab (1.27-1.65 eV) is resolved.
  3. Amorphous 2 nm versus amorphous bulk: whether the tail states follow the confined band edge. This is the dominant model-form uncertainty at 2 nm (onset 0.26 vs 0.91 V).
  4. A device-like Al2O3|IWO|OH termination, for dEc and the band offset to Al2O3 that the registered P8 Schrodinger-Poisson check needs.

Minimum ATLAS runs (57 of 57 launches used): 0 for the confinement and Qf update (exact identities); 1 plus 1 contingency to certify the 2 nm m*/Nc change; 0-2 conditional for the Pd barrier; 2 optional for P8. Six of 57 launches gave no currents, and the parallel pilot failed, so runs should be sequential. Any DFT insertion must be a separate V2 with its own register, done after the S12 comparison of the registered V1 predictions. V2 must start from the calibrated runs' material_model_used.json, not from config\ (the seed: Qf 0.0, mu 16.8).

findings.verdict: Valid substitution that adds no knob, but NOT an out-of-sample test on existing data; needs 0 ATLAS launches
findings.detail:
How it is set now: the deck sets AFFINITY = chi_bulk - dEc(t), giving 3.947 / 4.228 / 4.274 eV at 2 / 6.3 / 13.2 nm. Labels: dEc is DFT_PURE_IN2O3_PROXY with +/-50 % uncertainty; chi_bulk = 4.3 +/- 0.3 eV is LITERATURE_IWO from a different device.

Why it cannot be tested on ID-VG:
- An affinity change is an exact rigid translation: +/-0.100 V per 0.1 eV, SS unchanged, max |dlog Id| <= 1.6e-5.
- dEc is degenerate with the FITTED Qf (1.73e12 cm^-2, equivalent to 0.31 V) and the ASSUMED gate WF (4.7 +/- 0.2 eV, equivalent to +/-1.12e12 cm^-2). dEc(2 nm) = 0.353 eV is equivalent to 1.97e12 cm^-2.
- Inserting a DFT dEc therefore only moves the refitted Qf. The thresholds are neutral to confinement (one-offset rms 0.136 V with vs 0.133 V without).
- The package itself says 'Even a correct dEc is not identifiable from these data; it has value only together with an optical gap vs t'.
- The real falsifier is the optical or IPES gap (conclusions C3): Eg(2) - Eg(13.2) is expected at +0.2 to 0.45 eV and is falsified if below 0.1 eV.

No launch is needed: the substitution, the shared-Qf refit and the exact mu_band rescale can all be computed from runs 0038 / 0039 / 0040 / 0014 through the documented identities.

Eg(t) has zero leverage: holes are not solved, and Eg sets only n_i (~1e-10 to 1e-7 cm^-3) and the trap integration range ('transfer curves are insensitive to it').

findings.item: Which DFT confinement number goes into ATLAS (sub-band energy vs subthreshold-equivalent shift; law refit)
findings.verdict: Under-specified in the proposal; must be pre-registered
findings.detail:
The DFT slab conduction-band shift is an E1-like sub-band energy. A classical 3-D ATLAS model needs the subthreshold-equivalent shift dEc_eq = -kT ln[sum_i g2D,i kT exp(-E_i/kT) / (Nc t)]. This is about 0.04 V smaller at 2 nm and 0.01 V smaller at 6.3 nm.

V1 handles two density-of-states effects inconsistently: it uses E1-like shifts and separately raises Nc through m*(t) (Nc ratio 1.376, i.e. 8 mV).

Recommended mapping: compute dEc_eq(t) directly from the relaxed slab's sub-band ladder (E_i and in-plane mass) and keep Nc at the bulk mass. One DFT-derived quantity then replaces two proxies, with no new knob.

The current t^-1.38 law overshoots the infinite-well bound by x1.59 at 6.3 nm and x2.51 at 13.2 nm. A free-exponent refit through only the 1 and 2 nm DFT points would repeat that error. The refit must impose the effective-mass t^-2 asymptote; the S3 effective-width form gives 0.357 / 0.050 / 0.012 eV at 2 / 6.3 / 13.2 nm.

findings.item: dEc/dEv partition and vacuum alignment (Block 1 priority 2)
findings.verdict: Matters for chi only; absolute PBE EA/IP must not enter ATLAS; the alignment protocol has an unexplained anomaly
findings.detail:
What ATLAS uses: only dEc (dEc/dEg = 1 is ASSUMED, from Si2021). dEv has no TCAD leverage because the model is electrons-only. A partition of dEc/dEg = 0.6 would lower the realized 2 nm term by about 0.13 V (estimate), and Qf would absorb it again.

Why absolute EA/IP cannot be used:
- Only EA differences between equally terminated slabs (1 nm vs 2 nm) isolate confinement.
- Absolute EA/IP include the H-termination dipole: relaxation alone moved the 1 nm CBM by 0.50 eV and the VBM by 1.33 eV on the vacuum scale.
- PBE EA(1 nm) = 3.93 eV almost equals the ATLAS AFFINITY(2 nm) = 3.947 eV. This is a coincidence, not a validation.

What is still missing:
- The bulk two-step (macroscopic-average) alignment is not done yet.
- The W-doped 1 nm slab shows an unexplained rigid upshift of every level by 1.27-1.65 eV on the vacuum scale. Until that is explained, no vacuum-referenced quantity from doped, metallic or interface slabs (EA, dipole, Phi_B, work-function change) should be mapped to chi, Qf or a contact work function.
- The device termination (Al2O3 below, air/OH above) differs from the symmetric H/vacuum slab. S3 states these dipoles are unquantified and degenerate with WF, chi and Qf.

findings.item: 6.3 nm and 13.2 nm crystalline slabs as tests of the 6.3 nm offset and the 6.3->13.2 nm mobility step (Block 3)
findings.verdict: Almost no decision value for the TCAD questions: the outcome is already bounded
findings.detail:
Computed here from the per-film Qf of SYNTHESIS D3 (with / without confinement: 1.81 / 0.09 / 1.56 vs 0.048 / -0.27 / 1.434 e12 cm^-2) and q/Cox = 0.179 V per 1e12. Linear rigid superposition; an estimate.

Threshold offset:
- With Qf shared by 2 and 13.2 nm, the 6.3 nm miss = 0.181 V + (d2 + d13)/2 - d6, where d is the realized confinement shift.
- Closing it needs d6 of about 0.36 V or more (dEc(6.3) about 0.4 eV) with d2 >= d6, i.e. the same confinement at 6.3 nm as at 2 nm.
- The infinite-well upper bound at 6.3 nm is about 0.045 eV, and the S3 Schrodinger-Poisson value is 0.016-0.043 V.
- For any monotonic dEc(t) with d6 <= 0.045 V, the miss stays at 0.14-0.37 V (0.28-0.30 V with S3-central values).

Mobility:
- The m* law gives m*(6.3)/m*(13.2) = 1.033 (a 3 % Drude effect) against the x4.58 step. Even a 2x DFT error leaves it under 10 %.
- The report already rejects confinement for the 2 ~ 6.3 >> 13.2 pattern (<= 0.05 V vs 0.36 V needed).

Consequences:
- A ~500-atom 6.3 nm slab and a ~1000-atom 13.2 nm slab can only confirm a rejection that already exists.
- The 6.3 vs 13.2 nm dEc difference (about 0.02-0.03 eV, estimate) is close to the DFT tolerances (10 meV vacuum criterion; 0.1 eV reproduction criterion).
- The working hypothesis C1 (structural transition) cannot be tested with crystalline slabs; its falsifiers are GIXRD/TEM, gated Hall, and the muFE ratio vs temperature.

findings.verdict: Adds no knob, but leverage is second order; at most 1 launch (2 nm), and only if |dm*/m*| > ~5 %
findings.detail:
How it is set now: m* enters only through NC300 (3.27 / 2.55 / 2.44e18 cm^-3 at 2 / 6.3 / 13.2 nm). Label: MEASURED_RELATED_MATERIAL for the bulk 0.208 m0, plus a PBE increment.

Measured sensitivity (runs 0050 / 0051): m* x1.3 gives dVth = -44 / -29 mV, SS_cc -17.7 / -13.2 mV/dec and Ion +4.1 / +5.8 % at 2 / 13.2 nm. That is +14.9 mV of the 0.58 V threshold step (2.4 %).

From log-linear scaling of run_0050 (estimate): a +/-5 % m* change moves Vth by about +/-8 mV and the mid-window SS by about +/-3 mV/dec. Both are below the calibration residuals (+19 / +9 / -29 mV), so the change is not testable.

Conventions to pre-register:
- PBE bulk m* is 0.159 vs 0.208 m0 measured (-24 %).
- The additive increment (V1) and the ratio convention differ by 11 % at 1 nm (0.330 vs 0.368 m0, computed from the DFT values 0.281 / 0.159) and by about 5 % at 2 nm.

Weak out-of-sample content: refit WTA on the 2 nm deep SS, then predict the deep SS at 6.3 / 13.2 nm. The differential effect is about 5 mV/dec for x1.3, and the 13.2 nm SS depends on the floor subtraction (136.1 raw vs 91.8). At 6.3 / 13.2 nm the Nc term is only -0.008 / -0.002 V, so no launch is needed there.

findings.item: Phi_Bn -> contact boundary condition (Pd items of Blocks 1 and 2)
findings.verdict: The only DFT output that can enter without a new knob AND has a distinct non-rigid signature, but only after a CBM (not gap) correction and within a narrow decision window
findings.detail:
How it is set now: the Pd source/drain have no CONTACT statement, so they are ideal Ohmic (ASSUMED; no TLM data).

Correct insertion: CONTACT name=source/drain WORKFUN = chi_ATLAS(t) + Phi_Bn,corr, plus SURF.REC. Never insert the DFT Pd work function or the DFT E_F on the vacuum scale: that mixes a PBE absolute level with the literature chi (4.3 +/- 0.3 eV).

Gap correction:
- PBE places the CBM too low. HSE opens the bulk gap by 1.19 eV (0.920 -> 2.108 eV, norm-conserving), and how much of that shift falls on the CBM relative to the average potential is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA.
- Illustration only, not a computed value: a CBM correction of 0.4-0.6 eV would turn a PBE 'Ohmic' interface (E_F 0.4 eV above E_C, the literature CNL) into a barrier of 0.0-0.2 eV. The correction therefore decides the verdict.
- Cheap fix: a bulk HSE run with the macroscopic-average CBM offset (the 40-atom bulk HSE took 12 min on an H100). No Pd hybrid calculation is needed; Pd SG15 is not available locally.

Decision window (computed; thermionic only; A* = 120 x 0.257; conditional on the model): rho_c = 9.3e-9 Ohm cm^2 x exp(Phi/kT).
- The S5 bound Rsd W <~ 5e4 Ohm um at 2 nm (R_sh 8.2e4 Ohm/sq) gives rho_c <~ 7.6e-5 Ohm cm^2, i.e. Phi <~ 0.23 eV.
- rho_c <= 1e-5 (<= 1.3 % of R_on) gives Phi <= 0.18 eV, which cannot be told apart from Ohmic and is absorbed by mu_band.
- So: Phi_corr < 0.18 eV confirms V1 with 0 launches. Phi_corr of 0.18-0.23 eV is testable only with low-Vd ID-VD (registered Ohmic baseline run_0041: Id(0.1)/Id(0.05) = 1.80-1.97); those data are not in the package. Phi_corr > 0.23 eV contradicts the measured theta_net = -0.10 V^-1 at 2 nm unless tunnelling dominates.

Further caveats:
- Pd on a 2 nm film may metallize it, leaving no bulk-like interior to define E_C. The extraction method (potential line-up) must be pre-registered and cross-checked on a thicker slab.
- Epitaxial Pd on bixbyite (001) needs a strained or coincidence supercell, and the choice of termination (O- vs In-terminated, H removed) can move Phi by tenths of an eV. Bracket at least 2 terminations.
- The real contact is Pd on largely amorphous IWO after a 150 C RTA.
- ATLAS pitfall: the Pd electrodes touch the Air insulator region. INS.OHMIC defaults to true and can silently keep the contact Ohmic; check ^ins.ohmic and the log.

findings.item: 'DFT predicts Phi_Bn -> freeze in TCAD -> predict I_off -> compare' and the Block 2 off-current premise
findings.verdict: Falsified in advance; the premise is not supported by the package records
findings.detail:
1. No V1 run changed the source/drain contact potential. The only work-function runs (0048 / 0049) changed the TiN gate WF. 'Changing the contact potential brought the simulated off-current toward measurement' has no basis in RUN_INDEX.
2. The earlier Astra package did run Schottky S/D contacts (electron barrier 0.15 eV). Its off-state Id at Vg = -3 to -0.5 V was 1e-34 to 1e-53 A/um or exactly zero, against measured floors of 4.6e-15 / 1.5e-13 / 6.6e-12 A/um ('tiny signed depletion values do not reproduce the measured plateau'). The V1 calibrated runs report 17-39 non-positive native Id samples.
3. In drift-diffusion the ideal Ohmic contact is already the injection upper bound, so a DFT barrier can only lower the current.
4. In a 20 um long-channel accumulation TFT, the off-current is set by the gate-controlled channel barrier relative to the source Fermi level, not by Phi_Bn. The thermionic factors (48x for 0.1 eV, 2.3e3x for 0.2 eV; arithmetic correct) apply to a contact-limited on-current.
5. The floors do not depend on gate voltage: at 13.2 nm the floor changes by only x1.06 while Vgd goes from 1.2 to 3.7 V. They scale as t^3.78-3.85, and thermal generation is 13-17 decades short. The candidate is an ungated path or an instrument floor (C8), tested by IG/IS and an L-series.
6. The floor region is excluded from scoring (active = measured Id > 5x the off-band median), so I_off is outside the model's calibrated domain.

Conclusion: register 'Pd/V_O barrier lowering explains the floors' as falsified for any DFT Phi value within this drift-diffusion model, and spend no launches on it.

findings.item: Trap-assisted tunnelling Pd -> V_O defect -> IWO CB (Block 2)
findings.verdict: Adds at least 3 unconstrained knobs and is not a geometric floor path
findings.detail:
ATLAS has TRAP.TUNNEL / MASS.TUNNEL and CONTACT E.TUNNEL / ME.TUNNEL. They need a trap spectrum, a tunnelling mass and the local field. The package audit warns explicitly: 'do not turn it on to fit a floor'.

Tunnelling at the Pd edge enhances injection at the contact. It does not create conduction across a gate-depleted 20 um channel.

Density, energy and mass would all be fitted, so the result has no out-of-sample content.

findings.verdict: Cannot be inserted without fitting; also forbidden by the model's provenance rule and untestable at 2 nm
findings.detail:
Provenance rule: the config says '~2 % W' is a label 'never converted to a donor density'. Nd_eff (2.50 / 2.52 / 2.97e17 cm^-3) is a FITTED law and explicitly 'NOT W concentration'.

Leverage: Nd x2 gives -9 mV at 2 nm. The sensitivity is about 0.04 V per 1e18 cm^-3 at 2 nm, 0.151 V at 6.3 nm and 0.406 V at 13.2 nm, and a donor step at 13.2 nm is degenerate with dEc (C2).

Why neutral slab defects give no densities: an active donor density needs charged-defect formation energies, transition levels, the chemical potentials of the unknown sputter + 150 C RTA process, and compensation. None of these is in the neutral-first plan.

Consistency check (computed; 2 %-cation basis assumed, the basis is NOT DETERMINED):
- W is about 5.8e20 cm^-3, i.e. 1.2e14 W/cm^2 in 2 nm and up to 3.5e14 e/cm^2 as W6+.
- The gate can deplete at most about Cox(Vth + 3 V)/q, roughly 2e13 cm^-2.
- A literal ATLAS insertion of the 1 nm DFT picture (a W-5d donor level about 0.19 eV below the CB holding E_F) would make the 2 nm device impossible to turn off. At least about 94 % of W electrons must be compensated or inactive.

DFT can support the chapter-13 inference (localization or compensation) but cannot supply the number.

findings.item: Defect DOS -> g_t(E) (crystalline-slab V_O DOS used as the trap DOS of an amorphous film)
findings.verdict: Physically questionable; it would add knobs
findings.detail:
Concentration problem (computed): one V_O or W in the 176-atom 2 nm cell (10.336 x 10.335 A; 18.34 A between outer O layers) is 9.4e13 cm^-2, about 5.1e20 cm^-3. That is 25x the fitted Nt(2 nm) = 2e19, about 2000x Nd_eff and about 50x Qf. The 'defect state' is a dispersive impurity band, not a dilute trap. In the 1 nm slab it is about 1.2e21 cm^-3.

Energy problem:
- Kohn-Sham levels of neutral defects are not thermodynamic transition levels, and PBE (gap 0.89 eV) places V_O levels unreliably.
- The model's subthreshold behaviour comes from an exponential acceptor tail (WTA 40 meV) attributed to disorder. A few discrete crystalline defect levels cannot produce that.

What ATLAS needs: g_t(E) requires density, energy, width, donor/acceptor type and capture cross sections (sigma = 1e-15 is ASSUMED). DFT could supply at most an energy, and only from charged-defect calculations with finite-size corrections. The density would still be fitted.

The open feature in the trap inversion (states at Ec - 0.15 to -0.20 eV underestimated x2.2-2.8; a near-Ec band within 1-2 kT) needs about kT of energy resolution, which PBE crystalline defect levels do not have.

findings.item: Interface dipole -> Qf / V_FB (Al2O3/IWO, Block 1 items 14-15)
findings.verdict: Only relabels an existing fitted knob; no out-of-sample test on ID-VG; 0 launches
findings.detail:
How it is set now: Qf (1.73e12 cm^-2, FITTED) is 'an alignment absorber, not a charge'. It is degenerate with the gate WF (ASSUMED 4.7 eV, range 4.5-4.9 = +/-1.12e12 cm^-2) and chi_bulk (+/-0.3 eV). The combined absolute uncertainty is about +/-0.36 V (quadrature, estimate), larger than any plausible DFT dipole.

Why it cannot explain the 6.3 nm offset: a local interface dipole does not depend on thickness beyond about 1-2 nm, so it cannot produce the 6.3 nm-specific -1.64e12 cm^-2 (0.294 V). Inserting it is an exact rigid shift, computable by identity. It is falsifiable only with multi-EOT C-V (intercept vs slope) plus KPFM/UPS, and neither is available.

C9 (Qf = an ionized V_O layer) needs the V_O (2+/0) level and the segregation energy at the interface, i.e. charged-defect interface supercells, which the proposal postpones.

Better TCAD use of the Al2O3/IWO calculation:
- Compute dEc for the device-like asymmetric termination (Al2O3|IWO|OH, dipole-corrected).
- Compute the Al2O3 conduction-band offset. It would replace the ASSUMED 2.0 / 3.4 / 4.0 eV of the S3 Schrodinger-Poisson surrogate and feed the registered but untested P8 check.

findings.verdict: The most decision-relevant model-form question DFT can answer for TCAD, but only with pre-registered statistics; PBE localization caveat
findings.detail:
The dominant model-form uncertainty at 2 nm is the tail-energy reference under confinement. If the tail follows the confined edge, the onset shifts by 0.26 V; if it stays at the bulk edge, by 0.91 V. The report records this as 'not determined'.

What DFT can do here:
- Amorphous 2 nm slabs vs an amorphous bulk cell, aligned by the macroscopic-average potential, can measure whether IPR-localized tail states shift with dEc. Crystalline slabs cannot answer this.
- It can also give a CB-tail width to compare with WTA = 40 meV (FITTED). WTA +5 meV gives +7.5 mV/dec deep SS, and S4 disfavours 60 meV (SS_cc +126 mV/dec).

Pre-registration: WTA survives if the DFT tail width is 30-50 meV; above 60 meV it conflicts with the measured SS.

Caveats:
- 3 structures of about 200 atoms give few tail states. The statistical uncertainty of an exponential width must be shown (e.g. by bootstrap) before use.
- PBE delocalization underestimates localization.
- Melt-quench cooling rates differ from sputtering + RTA.

Insertion changes the deck form (tail referenced to a different edge): 1 launch at 2 nm, with Nt still fitted.

findings.item: HSE at 2 nm vs the hybrid correction actually needed for alignment
findings.verdict: Use bulk hybrid band-edge offsets; a 2 nm slab HSE run likely exceeds one H100 (estimate)
findings.detail:
Measured: the 1 nm slab HSE took 4.0 h with 40.6 GB of exact-exchange arrays.

Scaled estimate: exact-exchange memory scales with N_occ x N_grid, giving x(1328/624) x (45.18/34.87), about x2.76. That is about 112 GB, more than the 94 GB of an H100 NVL; time would be about x6, roughly one day.

For TCAD only the PBE/HSE shift ratio matters, and Qf absorbs it, so the 1 nm ratio (1.06-1.11) can be applied at 2 nm.

What every alignment-based mapping (chi, Phi_Bn, the Al2O3 band offset) actually lacks is the bulk CBM/VBM offset relative to the macroscopic-average potential, in both PBE and HSE. That is a 40-atom bulk calculation (12 min measured).

findings.item: Falsifiability procedure: registered predictions and the model state
findings.verdict: DFT insertion must be a forked V2 with its own register, done after the S12 comparison; config\ is not the calibrated state
findings.detail:
The register (2026-09-24T23:24:53Z, 44 hashed files) stays prospective only if the model state is unchanged and nothing is refit before the S12 (65 / 85 C) comparison. 'Any later change ... invalidates the prospective status.'

Chapter 13 plans to 'repeat the ATLAS campaign of the four thicknesses with the new laws'. That must not overwrite V1. The 31.8 nm film is out of scope (a documented failure), so no launch should be spent there.

config\iwo_material_model.yaml is the seed, not the calibrated state:
- It has fixed_interface_charge_Qf_cm2 = 0.0 and mu_band 2.0 nm = 16.8.
- The calibrated run_0038 material_model_used.json has Qf = 1.73e12 and mu_band = 17.69 (final 17.6897).
- A V2 built from config\ without the stage overrides would silently drop 0.31 V of rigid shift.

Base V2 on the material_model_used.json of runs 0038-0040, plus 0014 for the 6.3 nm shared-parameter case.

findings.item: Minimum ATLAS re-run set (budget: 57 of 57 launches used)
findings.verdict: 1 launch (+1 contingency) covers the DFT confinement/mass update; the Pd barrier adds 0-2 conditional launches; V_O/W/TAT runs are not recommended
findings.detail:
Tier 0 (0 launches): substitute dEc_eq(t), refit the shared Qf and rescale mu_band using the exact identities (affinity and Qf rigid to 1.6e-5 dec; Id proportional to mu to 6e-6) on runs 0038 / 0039 / 0040 and 0014. This gives the V2 thresholds and the recomputed 6.3 nm miss (pre-registered 0.14-0.37 V).

Tier 1 (1 launch, 2 nm): certify the non-rigid Nc part with the DFT m*(2 nm). Skip it if |dm*/m*| <= 5 %.

Tier 2 (0-2 launches, conditional): Pd barrier at 2 nm, as ID-VG at Vd = 0.7 V plus ID-VD at Vg 1-3 V. Run it only if Phi_Bn,corr is about 0.18-0.30 eV AND measured ID-VD for that device is obtained (the package holds only ID-VG at Vd = 0.7 V). Verify that WORKFUN is actually applied (INS.OHMIC).

Tier 3 (2 launches, optional): the registered P8 Schrodinger-Poisson/BQP check at 6.3 and 13.2 nm with DFT m* and the Al2O3 band offset. This is the only DFT-fed run aimed at the unexplained 6.3 nm shape part.

Contingency and execution:
- 6 of 57 launches produced no currents (0010, 0011, 0018, 0053, 0056, 0057), about 11 %, so add +1.
- The parallel pilot (0056 / 0057, started in the same second) failed on both runs, so run sequentially.
- RUN_INDEX labels both 0056 and 0057 as 'launch 56/57' (a bookkeeping slip).

Request now: 2 launches (Tier 1 + contingency); up to 6 if the Tier 2 / 3 conditions are met.

Not recommended: V_O/W -> N_D, g_t(E) and trap-assisted tunnelling hypotheses. Each costs at least 3 launches (one per film) and adds at least 2 fitted parameters, so there is no net falsification.

findings.item: Proposed pre-registered acceptance numbers (what each DFT result must be for its hypothesis to survive)
findings.verdict: Proposed register; computed from package numbers and labelled as estimates
findings.detail:
(a) V1 confinement law at 2 nm: survives if the HSE-corrected dEc_eq(2 nm) realizes 0.315 +/- 0.06 V in ATLAS (roughly dEg_PBE(2 nm) = 0.33 +/- 0.07 eV with dEc/dEg >= 0.8). Otherwise revise by identity and report the change in shared Qf (about dV/0.179 V per 1e12 cm^-2).
(b) Confinement explains the 6.3 nm rigid offset: needs realized d6 >= ~0.36 V with d2 >= d6 and d13 ~ 0. Rejected in advance: the infinite-well bound at 6.3 nm is ~0.045 eV.
(c) Confinement contributes to the 6.3 -> 13.2 nm mobility step: needs m*(6.3)/m*(13.2) ~ 4.6. Rejected in advance: the law gives 1.033.
(d) Ohmic Pd at 2 nm: survives if Phi_Bn,corr <= 0.18 eV; testable between 0.18 and 0.23 eV; above 0.23 eV it contradicts the theta bound (thermionic estimate).
(e) S5 M2 (confinement raises the Pd barrier at 2 nm): survives only if the corrected E_F(Pd) lies below E_C(2 nm), i.e. dEc(2 nm) > E_CNL - E_C,bulk (literature 0.4 eV). With dEc(2 nm) ~ 0.33 eV it is expected to fail.
(f) Pd/V_O barrier lowering explains the off-floors: falsified in advance for any Phi.
(g) W is an active donor at roughly the W content: falsified in advance by the device turning off (at least ~94 % of W electrons inactive).
(h) Qf = interface dipole or an ionized V_O layer: not testable on ID-VG. For C9 to survive, DFT must give a charged interface V_O whose (2+/0) level lies above E_F at threshold (~Ec - 0.04 eV), with a negative segregation energy. The test is C-V.
(i) WTA is a physical disorder width: the amorphous DFT CB-tail width is 30-50 meV; above 60 meV it conflicts.
(j) For experiment: register Eg(2) - Eg(13.2) = HSE-corrected dEg(2 nm) minus ~0.01-0.03 eV; falsified if the measured value is below 0.1 eV (C3).

findings.item: Which open questions in chapters 08-12 the proposed DFT actually tests
findings.verdict: Directly: C3 (only together with an optical gap), the S5-M2 Pd barrier, and the tail-reference model form. Partly: C6 / WTA and P8. Not at all: C1, C2, C4, C5, C7, C8, C10 and the 6.3 nm rigid offset
findings.detail:
Not addressed by the proposed DFT:
- 6.3 nm rigid offset (0.294 V): bounded away (see the 6.3 / 13.2 nm finding). C4 (device spread / sweep history) needs replicates.
- 6.3 nm shape part (C5, density-dependent mobility; ranked first): no crystalline DFT output enters. DFT m* and the band offset only feed the third-ranked candidate, field quantization (P8).
- C1 structural transition: needs structure data; crystalline slabs are mute.
- C2 donor step at 13.2 nm: DFT gives no densities.
- C7 near-Ec band (1-2 kT): beyond PBE resolution.
- C8 off-floors: need IG/IS and an L-series; DFT is irrelevant.
- C10 MTR temperature behaviour: the S12 comparison, which needs no DFT.

Addressed:
- C3 confinement: DFT narrows the number; the falsifier is the optical gap.
- S5 M2 Pd barrier: Pd/2 nm Phi_Bn, with low-Vd ID-VD as the experiment.
- C6 surface + bulk DOS and the WTA physics: only through amorphous slabs, with statistics.
- C9 Qf = V_O layer: only with charged interface defects.

top_recommendations: First run the zero-launch S12 (65/85 C) comparison of the registered V1 predictions. Only after that, fork a V2 model with its own timestamped register. Build V2 from the material_model_used.json of runs 0038-0040 (and 0014), not from config\iwo_material_model.yaml: the config is the seed, with Qf = 0.0 and mu = 16.8.

Put the DFT confinement into ATLAS as the subthreshold-equivalent shift computed from the relaxed slab's sub-band ladder, with Nc kept at the bulk mass. Impose the effective-mass t^-2 asymptote instead of a free-exponent 2-point refit. Apply it, plus the shared-Qf refit and the exact mu rescale, by identity (0 launches). Request 1 launch plus 1 contingency, run sequentially, only to certify the 2 nm m*/Nc change if |dm*/m*| > 5 %.

Drop 'Phi_Bn -> freeze -> predict I_off' and the Pd/V_O off-floor mini-campaign as TCAD tests; register them as falsified in advance. The V1 Ohmic contact is already the injection upper bound, the 20 um off-state is set by the channel barrier, the earlier Astra Schottky runs gave 1e-34 to 1e-53 A/um against floors of 4.6e-15 to 6.6e-12 A/um, and the floors need IG/IS plus an L-series.

Before any Pd interface calculation: compute the bulk PBE and HSE CBM/VBM offsets relative to the macroscopic-average potential (40-atom bulk, minutes on GPU), and explain the 1.27-1.65 eV vacuum-level shift of the W-doped slab. Pre-register the Phi_Bn decision window: below 0.18 eV keep Ohmic; 0.18-0.23 eV is testable only with low-Vd ID-VD; above 0.23 eV is inconsistent with the 2 nm theta bound unless tunnelling dominates. Insert it as WORKFUN = chi_ATLAS(t) + Phi_Bn,corr, checking INS.OHMIC.

Do not map V_O/W slab results to N_D or g_t(E): the slab concentrations are about 5e20 cm^-3, neutral Kohn-Sham levels are not transition levels, and the densities would be fitted. Use the W results only as qualitative support for a compensated, fitted Nd_eff. A literal insertion would stop the 2 nm device from turning off.

Remove 6.3 nm and 13.2 nm crystalline slabs from the TCAD-motivated list; their outcome is already bounded (infinite-well dEc(6.3) <= 0.045 eV against about 0.36 V needed; m* ratio 1.03 against x4.6). Spend thickness-related DFT on (a) amorphous 2 nm vs amorphous bulk tail reference and width, with pre-registered statistics, and (b) a device-like Al2O3|IWO|OH slab for dEc and the Al2O3 band offset feeding the registered P8 Schrodinger-Poisson check (2 optional launches).

Register the experimental falsifiers that DFT outputs actually feed, and request the data per LAB_DATA_REQUEST.md: the optical-gap shift Eg(2) - Eg(13.2) (falsified below 0.1 eV), V_FB(t) from multi-EOT C-V for any dipole or Qf claim, and low-Vd ID-VD at 2 nm for the Pd barrier.
